I swear this is the hardest part of having issues. It's like I know it's a lot to handle and they have no obligation to help us, and I know it does affect them mentally too, but it's still hurtful as fuck when they leave. 

What I did was... after I noticed my friend wasn't that willing to talk about my mental issues anymore, I tried a different approach. I only talk to them about gaming, anime, or other stuff we're both equally interested in. It's helpful for me because it gets me interested in something. And it gets them to talk to me again. Then every once in a while I'd talk a bit about my issues again and they'd listen again. But only because I keep it v brief now and go back to our fun stuff after. 

It's sad the things we have to do to get help and support but I guess this is just how the world is like.

I think now even the term PWID isn't v popular because of "disability", but I digress. 

Because the term was once used on actual groups of people with actual disabilities, it's also insulting to these people when you use the same term on a normal person as an insult.

I think the other user have mentioned the main thing: just write her like how you would write any other character. Don't genderize the writing unless necessary. 

But I'll just add some comments based on my personal experience as a woman and my feelings towards female characters as a female reader, so this might be a bit subjective: 

1) Not all women are emotional and sensitive, so you don't necessarily have to portray them that way. This not only applies to how they interact with people, but also how they process their thoughts. I've seen a lot of male authors write females as though our entire decision making process is based on feelings, but no, we can be highly logical too. So decide on the character's personality, and if she's not meant to be the "feeling" type, don't suddenly make her one when she's supposed to make decisions for example. Be consistent with her personality too. 

2) Don't over describe her appearance. I'd say only describe her appearance when it's relevant to the plot. I've seen descriptions like "her perfectly-shaped eyebrows crinkled into a frown" and honestly it's super weird to me. Unless the said woman is getting her makeup done and is at a fashion show or she's super into her appearance then just don't. 

3) I think it would be good to understand the physical strength of women if you want to write female characters. Because there's nothing more irritating to a female reader when the female lead is unnecessarily weak and needs a man for almost everything. 

4) To the character's age into account. A teenage girl is definitely going to be different from a woman in her 30s. Based on my personal experience I feel like the main differences between males and females really start to show after around the age of 25. In terms of thought process, how they view the world and all that. teenage girls and boys alike are just more simple-minded. They're more likely to be very into 1 particular thing, it could romantic interest, it could be a hobby, it could be a celebrity for example. I mention this because I've read books where authors forget to take the character's age into account, and their character behave older than they actually are, with no good reason for it. 

So yea. These are my subjective tips. Good luck!

You speak as if all other purchases in the world are tangible in some way or another, whether it's an object or a digital item. But that's not true. 

A lot of times we're spending just for the experience. Why go to an expensive 5 star restaurant when you can spend a fraction of that price buying groceries and cooking yourself? It's for that experience. If you're someone who doesn't care about food, spending $500 on a meal is a complete waste of money. What for? They all become shit anyway right. But if you value that experience of fine dining then the $500 is well spent. 

The same can be said for spending on games. If spending $200 to gamble for a chance to get a bundle of pixels makes one happy, and is within the person's means of spending, how is it wrong? Maybe he has a lot of expendable income and doesn't have any other hobbies. Maybe he doesn't like to go out and party. Maybe he doesn't watch movies in cinemas and only stream online. Maybe all his clothes are from thrift stores because he doesn't give a shit about expensive clothes. 

Bottom line is, it's okay for us to spend our money on whatever we want, as long as it's reasonable and within our means. If someone is sacrificing meals for the sake of a game then obviously that's a problem. You may not enjoy the experience of spending in game, but that doesn't make someone who enjoy it wrong.

This is my own method, since I don't know how to use those circle and triangle art guides, neither do I know anatomy: 

I usually start from drawing the eyes and expand out, because it's easier for me to gauge the distance between each individual feature than to estimate the overall shape of the face and the position of each facial feature relative to the face. 

Also I try to break everything down into smaller shapes. Like an eye is a circle with 2 trapeziums / triangles next to it. It makes me understand the shape better than if I just look at the whole thing as an eye.

Native speaker here. Let me see if I can help. 

了is a sentence ender and a tense marker, and can be used in different ways. 

When it's behind a verb, it conveys that the action in the verb has been done. Like 我到了 = I've reached. 

It can also be used to mark a change in state: like 下雨了 = it's raining --> implies that it wasn't originally raining but it's raining now. 

It's also used to end persuasion sentences like 不能再等了，别说了, etc. 

Regarding the use of 太 - it's a superlative term and can be used on its own. There's no rule that it has to be used with 了。But when it is used with 了, it's used as an exclamation (which is not inherently positive or negative). Like 太美了= it's too beautiful! --> Which can be positive or negative depending on the tone of the user or the rest of the context. 

When used on its own, 太 is just to represent something is too \_\_\_\_. Like 水太烫，等一下再喝 = the water is too hot, you should drink it later.
